2027-03-25.alt: Hasha Week. Pesaha: only one Holy Qurbana is celebrated in each church, with the Order of the third Qudasha (named in the calendar after Mar Nestorius); outside the Qurbana, Holy Communion is given today only to the sick. The Annunciation (25 March) falls on Pesaha this year and is transferred as the Syro-Malabar Ordo directs (verify locally); in the Latin calendar it moves to Monday 5 April.
2027-03-25.verse: Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.
theo: Pesaha is the Aramaic and Syriac form of the Hebrew Pesach, the Passover. For the St Thomas Christians the word names this whole holy Thursday: the night the Lord ate the Passover with his disciples, gave us the Holy Qurbana and the priesthood, and washed their feet. Tonight every parish gathers around one altar, and every home around one table. The first reading takes us back to the night in Egypt. “This month shall mark for you the beginning of months”: the Passover begins a new year and a new life. Each household is to take “a lamb for each family”, and if a household is too small, “it shall join its closest neighbor”. The lamb must be “without blemish, a year-old male”. At twilight it is slaughtered, and its blood is put “on the two doorposts and the lintel of the houses in which they eat it.” They eat it “roasted over the fire with unleavened bread and bitter herbs”, dressed for a journey: “your loins girded, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you shall eat it hurriedly. It is the passover of the LORD.” God promises, “when I see the blood, I will pass over you”, and he commands, “This day shall be a day of remembrance for you.” For seven days no leaven may be found in their houses. Every detail points to tonight. Jesus is the Lamb without blemish, whom John the Baptist had called “the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world” (John 1:29), and Paul writes, “For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed” (1 Corinthians 5:7). The unleavened bread of Israel's haste becomes the unleavened appam of our Pesaha table, and the memorial of the Exodus becomes the memorial of a greater exodus: from sin and death to the Father.

The second reading, from the last of the prophets, is a sharp rebuke. The priests of Malachi's time offered God what they would not have dared to offer a governor, bringing as their offering “what has been taken by violence or is lame or sick”, and they treated the Lord's table with contempt. God cries out: “Oh, that someone among you would shut the temple doors, so that you would not kindle fire on my altar in vain!” Then comes a promise that looks far beyond Jerusalem: “For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering”. From the first century the Church heard in these words a prophecy of the Holy Qurbana. The Didache, one of the oldest Christian writings, recalls Malachi when it tells believers to confess their sins and be reconciled before they break bread on the Lord's Day, so that their sacrifice may be pure; St Justin and St Irenaeus taught that the pure offering made in every place is the Eucharist of the Church among the nations. When the Pesaha Qurbana is celebrated tonight in Kerala, in the Gulf, in Europe, in America and in Australia, from the rising of the sun to its setting, Malachi's word is fulfilled. His warning also stands: the Lord deserves our best and not what is left over, and we come to his altar tonight with hearts made clean.

Paul gives us the oldest written account of the Supper, set down about twenty-five years after that night: “For I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night when he was betrayed took a loaf of bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and said, ‘This is my body that is for you. Do this in remembrance of me.’ In the same way he took the cup also, after supper, saying, ‘This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me.’” Matthew, read together with John tonight, gives the words of the covenant: “Take, eat; this is my body.” “Drink from it, all of you; for this is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.” Jesus does not say: this is a sign of my body. He says: this is my body. The Church has always believed that by the word of Christ and the power of the Holy Spirit the bread and wine become truly, really and substantially his Body and Blood (Catechism 1374–1376), and that the Qurbana is the memorial of his sacrifice, in which the one sacrifice of the Cross is made present (Catechism 1362–1367). That is why Paul is so serious: “For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.” And: “Examine yourselves, and only then eat of the bread and drink of the cup. For all who eat and drink without discerning the body, eat and drink judgment against themselves.” Tonight we also thank God for the priesthood. When Jesus said, Do this in remembrance of me, he made his apostles priests of the new covenant (Catechism 611, 1337). Then, Matthew tells us, “When they had sung the hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.” The Supper leads straight to Gethsemane and the Cross.

John, who does not tell of the bread and the cup, tells instead what Jesus did at the same table. “Now before the festival of the Passover, Jesus knew that his hour had come to depart from this world and go to the Father. Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.” Knowing “that the Father had given all things into his hands”, the Lord of all “got up from the table, took off his outer robe, and tied a towel around himself. Then he poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples' feet”. In that world it was the work of a slave. Peter protests: “You will never wash my feet.” Jesus answers: “Unless I wash you, you have no share with me.” Peter, all or nothing as always, cries: “Lord, not my feet only but also my hands and my head!” Jesus washes even the feet of Judas, knowing who was to betray him. Then he sits down again and explains: “So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet. For I have set you an example, that you also should do as I have done to you.” By reading John and Matthew together tonight, the Syro-Malabar Church teaches us that the altar and the basin belong together. The One who gives us his Body and Blood is the One who kneels at our feet. A Qurbana that does not lead us to serve has not yet reached our hands and feet.

How the parish keeps Pesaha, step by step (customs vary; follow your own parish). First, one Qurbana: in each church only one Holy Qurbana is celebrated today, usually in the afternoon or evening, so that the whole parish gathers around one altar as the apostles gathered around one table. The calendar directs the Order of the third Qudasha, used only on a few great days of the year. Outside this Qurbana, Holy Communion is taken today only to the sick. Second, the Word: the four readings are proclaimed, the Passover lamb, Malachi's pure offering, Paul's account of the Supper, and the Gospel of the washing of the feet and the institution. Third, the washing of the feet: usually after the Gospel and the homily, the celebrant lays aside his outer vestment, ties a towel around himself and kneels before twelve persons chosen from the parish, who represent the apostles. He pours water over the feet of each, dries them and kisses them, while the choir sings the hymns of the Lord's humility. Watch the priest kneel, and remember who knelt first. Fourth, the Qurbana continues: the gifts are brought to the altar, the anaphora is prayed, and the Lord's own words over the bread and the cup are spoken on the very night on which he first spoke them. Fifth, Communion: prepare with a good confession, and receive with reverence, discerning the body. Sixth, the watch: in many parishes the Blessed Sacrament is honoured with adoration far into the night, in answer to the Lord's question in Gethsemane: “So, could you not stay awake with me one hour?” (Matthew 26:40). Come for at least one hour.

How the family keeps Pesaha at home, step by step. The Syro-Malabar home has its own Pesaha, cherished for generations, which many see as a living echo of Israel's Passover meal. First, the appam: during the day the mother of the family, often with the children, prepares the Pesaha appam, an unleavened bread of rice flour (in many places with roasted urad dal and grated coconut), steamed and never leavened, because the Lord ate the Passover with unleavened bread. The little cross made from Hosanna Sunday's palm is pressed on top. In many places it is called the INRI appam, from the letters placed above the Cross. Second, the paal: Pesaha paal is coconut milk boiled with jaggery and a little cardamom or dry ginger, sweet and dark, to be eaten with the appam. Third, the gathering: in the evening, after the parish Qurbana, the whole family gathers around the table or on a mat, with a lamp lit. Fourth, prayer and the Word: the head of the family leads the prayers, the account of the Supper or of the washing of the feet is read (John 13 or 1 Corinthians 11), and the family sings a hymn and prays a psalm. Fifth, the breaking: the father, or the eldest member, breaks the appam, dips each piece in the paal and gives it to each member of the household in order of age. Sixth, the meaning: this is not a Qurbana and not a second Eucharist, but a family memorial and a holy custom, which gathers the house around the Lord's Supper that the parish has just celebrated. In many places a house in mourning does not make its own appam that year, and neighbours or relatives share theirs with it. In the Gulf and in distant lands, families who cannot find all the old ingredients keep the custom anyway, and children who have never seen Kerala learn this night by heart.
conn: The Hebrew Pesach means passing over (Exodus 12:13); the Syriac Pesaha gives its name to this Thursday and to the appam and paal of the home.
No bone of the Passover lamb was to be broken (Exodus 12:46); John sees this fulfilled on the Cross: “None of his bones shall be broken” (John 19:36).
Paul tells Christians to celebrate the festival not with the old yeast of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth (1 Corinthians 5:8).
Malachi 1:11 is quoted in the Didache (chapter 14) and by St Justin and St Irenaeus as a prophecy of the Eucharist offered among the nations.
Moses sealed the covenant with blood at Sinai (Exodus 24:8); Jeremiah promised a new covenant (Jeremiah 31:31); Jesus says, This is my blood of the covenant (Matthew 26:28).
At the Passover meal the Hallel psalms (Psalms 113–118) were sung; among them Psalm 116, I will lift up the cup of salvation, which Jesus would have sung with his disciples on this night.
At the Supper Jesus says, I am among you as one who serves (Luke 22:27); he came not to be served but to serve (Mark 10:45).
The Word was made flesh in Mary's womb so that he could give his flesh for the life of the world (John 6:51); the feast is transferred this year, but the two mysteries belong together.
altar: Tonight at the Holy Qurbana the Lord's words are spoken on the night on which he first spoke them: This is my body; this is my blood. What he did in the upper room, he does on our altar.
The Lamb whose blood marked the doorposts in Egypt is the Lamb on our altar; the blood of the new covenant is not put on our doors but given to us to drink.
Malachi's pure offering is made tonight from the rising of the sun to its setting, wherever the Syro-Malabar Church celebrates the Pesaha Qurbana.
outline: Ask: what does it mean that the Lord loved his own to the end, and that I am one of his own?
Point 1 · The blood on the doorposts
The Passover lamb and our paschal Lamb.
Point 2 · A pure offering in every place
Malachi's promise and the Qurbana of the nations.
The Real Presence, the sacrifice, the priesthood.
The altar and the basin belong together.
A priest kneeling with a towel and a basin, and a father breaking the Pesaha appam for his children.
“Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.”
live: Let the whole family come together to the Pesaha Qurbana of your parish, and arrive early.
If you have not yet made your confession, make it before the Qurbana, and receive Communion with reverence.
Prepare the appam and paal together, read John 13 at the table, and let the eldest break the bread for all.
Do one humble service at home tonight that is usually left to someone else, without being asked.
Spend an hour in adoration before the Blessed Sacrament tonight, or a quiet hour of prayer at home.
fathers: It is not a man who makes the gifts become the Body and Blood of Christ, but Christ himself, who was crucified for us. The priest stands there fulfilling the figure and speaking the words; the power and the grace are God's. This is my body, he says, and that word transforms the gifts.
Do not regard the bread and wine as plain bread and wine, for they are the Body and Blood of Christ, as the Lord has declared. Even if the senses suggest otherwise, let faith make you firm.
In your bread is hidden the Spirit who is not consumed; in your wine dwells the fire that is not drunk. The Lord who washed the feet of his disciples gave them his own Body with the same hands.
The Lord washed the feet of his disciples to teach us that we must do for one another what he did for us; and he gave us his Body so that we, many as we are, may become one body.
magis: The Lord, having loved those who were his own, loved them to the end. Knowing that the hour had come, he washed their feet and gave the commandment of love, and he instituted the Eucharist as the memorial of his death and Resurrection.

By celebrating the Last Supper with his apostles in the course of the Passover meal, Jesus gave the Jewish Passover its definitive meaning: his passing over to the Father by his death and Resurrection.
The Eucharist is a sacrifice because it makes present the sacrifice of the Cross; the sacrifice of Christ and the sacrifice of the Eucharist are one single sacrifice.
In the Eucharist the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, together with his soul and divinity, and therefore the whole Christ, is truly, really and substantially contained.
By the words Do this in remembrance of me, Jesus instituted his apostles as priests of the New Covenant.
Taking part in the Eucharistic sacrifice, the source and summit of the whole Christian life, the faithful offer the divine Victim to God, and themselves along with it.
saints: This year 25 March falls on Pesaha. The feast of the Annunciation is transferred as the Syro-Malabar Ordo directs (verify locally); in the Latin calendar it is kept on Monday 5 April 2027.

26 Mar: Passion Friday (Dukha Velli), with fasting and abstinence, the bitter drink (kaippuneer), the Way of the Cross and the veneration of the Cross. 27 Mar: Great Saturday. 28 Mar: Easter, the Uyirppu of the Lord.
2027-03-25.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Lamb of God without blemish, on the night you were betrayed you took bread and the cup and gave us your Body and Blood, and you knelt to wash the feet of your disciples. Having loved your own, you loved them to the end. Make us worthy to receive you tonight with clean hearts, discerning your Body. Bless the priests you have chosen to do this in your memory. Teach us to wash one another's feet, to watch with you in Gethsemane, and to follow you through the Cross to the joy of your Resurrection. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

quick: The Passover lamb, whose blood saved Israel, points to Christ, our paschal Lamb.
On the night he was betrayed Jesus said: This is my body; this is my blood of the covenant. He gave us the Holy Qurbana and the priesthood.
The Lord and Teacher washed his disciples' feet: the altar and the basin belong together.
2027-03-25.action: Come to the one Pesaha Qurbana with your whole family, and break the Pesaha appam at home tonight.
2027-03-25.question: Do I receive the Lord's Body with a heart that discerns him and with hands ready to serve?
catechism: The Lord loved his own to the end and instituted the Eucharist.
The Real Presence of Christ in the Eucharist.
The institution of the priesthood at the Last Supper.
kidsaint: A boy in Rome about 1,700 years ago who carried the Holy Eucharist to Christians in prison. When some people tried to snatch it from him, he held Jesus close to his heart and would not let go, and he died protecting him. Lesson: Jesus in the Holy Qurbana is our greatest treasure!
2027-03-25.special: Pesaha Thursday: Holy Qurbana of the Lord's Supper, washing of the feet, Pesaha appam and paal at home. The Annunciation is transferred this year.
term: The Syriac form of Pesach, Passover. For the St Thomas Christians it names Holy Thursday, the day of the Lord's Supper, and the Pesaha appam and paal shared by the family that night.

family.explain: On the night before he died, Jesus had a special supper with his friends. He took bread and said: this is my body. He took the cup and said: this is my blood. That is how he gave us the Holy Qurbana. Then he did something surprising: he knelt down and washed his friends' feet, like a servant. He said: I have given you an example; you also should do as I have done. Tonight we break the Pesaha appam together to remember his love.
family.intention: We pray for our priests, for families who cannot be together tonight, and for homes in mourning.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us serve someone in our family tonight, as Jesus washed his friends' feet?”

illus: In a parish near Kanjirappally, the vicar had a hard year: a senior parishioner had opposed him at every parish council meeting and spoken against him in the town. When the list for the washing of the feet was drawn up, the vicar quietly added that man's name. At the Pesaha Qurbana the old man saw the priest kneel before him with the basin, and his face went red. The priest washed his feet, dried them and kissed them. After the Qurbana the man came to the sacristy, could not say anything, and simply took the priest's hand. That night he sent a piece of his family's Pesaha appam to the parish house.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you loved your own to the end. Be among us now as one who serves, and teach us to love as you have loved. Amen.
share: The blood shall be a sign for you (Exodus 12:13). What does the blood of the Lamb mean for my home and my family?
in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering (Malachi 1:11). Do I bring the Lord my best or what is left over?
This is my body that is for you (1 Corinthians 11:24). How do I prepare to receive the Lord, discerning his Body?
you also ought to wash one another's feet (John 13:14). Whose feet is the Lord asking me to wash?
pm.resp: Lord, you loved us to the end.
interc: For the Church, gathered tonight around one altar in every place.
For our bishops and priests, on the night the Lord instituted the priesthood.
For families who cannot be together tonight, for migrants far from home, and for homes in mourning.
For the sick who receive Holy Communion at home today, and for all who cannot come to the Qurbana.
For the Jewish people, who keep the Passover, and for all who hunger for the Bread of Life.
For our group, that we may serve one another as the Lord served us.
pm.close: Father, on the night before he suffered your Son gave us the sacrament of his Body and Blood and the example of his love. Keep us faithful to his memory, make us one at his altar, and send us out to wash one another's feet. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, tonight is Pesaha. In Egypt, on the night of the Passover, each family took a lamb without blemish, put its blood on the doorposts, and ate it with unleavened bread, ready for the journey. God said: when I see the blood, I will pass over you (Exodus 12:13). That night became a day of remembrance for ever.

Tonight the true Lamb sits at table with his friends. Our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed (1 Corinthians 5:7). His blood is not painted on our doors; he gives it to us to drink. And Malachi's promise is fulfilled: from the rising of the sun to its setting a pure offering is made to God's name, at every altar where the Qurbana is celebrated.

On the night he was betrayed, the Lord took bread, gave thanks, broke it and said: this is my body that is for you. Do this in remembrance of me. He took the cup and said: this is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. He did not say this is a sign. He said this is my body. That is the faith of the Church: Christ is truly present, and his one sacrifice is made present on our altar.

Tonight we thank God for our priests. When the Lord said, Do this in remembrance of me, he made his apostles priests of the new covenant. Pray for the priest who will stand at our altar tonight, and for the priests who baptized you and absolved you.

Then the Lord did something no master ever did. He got up from the table, tied a towel around himself, and washed his disciples' feet, even the feet of Judas. Peter said: you will never wash my feet. Jesus said: unless I wash you, you have no share with me (John 13:8). We too must let him wash us, in confession and in his mercy.

And he said: if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet (John 13:14). The altar and the basin belong together. Tonight, when the priest kneels before twelve of our people, remember who knelt first; and tomorrow, in your home and your work, kneel in the same way.

Tonight we will break the Pesaha appam in our homes, dip it in the paal and share it from the eldest to the youngest. It is not a second Qurbana, but it keeps our homes united around the Lord's Supper. Then let us not sleep too soon. The Lord asks: could you not stay awake with me one hour? Let us watch with him. Having loved his own, he loved them to the end. Amen.
kids: Children, at the Last Supper Jesus gave us himself in the Holy Qurbana. He said: this is my body. That is why we are so quiet and careful when we receive him!
Then Jesus washed his friends' feet, like a servant. Tonight, can you help at home without being asked, to show Jesus' love?

intro: On this night three disciples show us three ways to stand before the Lord's love: Judas who leaves, Peter who resists, and the beloved disciple who rests on his heart.

points.h: Judas: the one who went out
sub: The devil had already put it into his heart.
points.apply: Bring to confession the sins you have been hiding.

sub: You will never wash my feet.
Then, Lord, not my feet only.
points.apply: Let the Lord serve you through the sacraments and through others.

points.h: The beloved disciple: the one who stayed close
sub: He will stand at the cross tomorrow.
points.apply: Spend some time tonight in adoration, close to the Lord.

concl: The Lord loves all three to the end.
We choose whether to go out into the night, to resist, or to stay close.
opts.resolve: Tonight I will stay close to the Lord in adoration, and I will let him wash me in confession.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the Gospel of this holy night begins: having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end (John 13:1). Around that table sat twelve men he loved. Tonight let us look at three of them.

The first is Judas. The devil had already put it into his heart to betray him (John 13:2). And yet Jesus knelt before him too and washed his feet. The Psalm had said: even my bosom friend in whom I trusted, who ate of my bread, has lifted the heel against me (Psalm 41:9). Later, Judas went out, and the Gospel adds: it was night. The tragedy of Judas is not only that he sinned, but that he hid his sin and walked away from the light.

The second is Peter. When Jesus came to him he said: you will never wash my feet. Pride does not want to be served. Jesus answered: unless I wash you, you have no share with me. And Peter said: Lord, not my feet only but also my hands and my head (John 13:8–9). Peter had faults, but he let the Lord come close. Like Isaiah, whose lips were touched by the burning coal, he was cleansed because he allowed it.

The third is the beloved disciple, reclining next to Jesus (John 13:23). He did not say much. He stayed close and listened to the heart of the Master. Tomorrow he will be the only apostle at the foot of the Cross, with Mary. Love is strong as death, says the Song of Songs (Song of Solomon 8:6).

Tonight the Lord gives us his Body and Blood at the Holy Qurbana. Which disciple will I be? Let me not go out into the night with hidden sins; let me bring them to confession. Let me not resist his service. Let me stay close to his heart in adoration tonight, and tomorrow stand with Mary and John at the Cross. Amen.

opts.a: The new covenant in his blood
intro: The first Passover was eaten in haste with unleavened bread. Tonight Christ gives a new Passover and a new covenant, and asks us to keep the feast with sincerity and truth.

sub: Paul: Christ our Passover is sacrificed.
points.apply: Remove one old habit of sin from your life this Holy Week.

points.h: The new covenant in my blood
sub: A covenant sealed in his own blood.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises tonight before the Blessed Sacrament.

points.h: Proclaiming the Lord's death until he comes
points.apply: Prepare for Easter Communion with a good confession.

concl: The Lord gives a new Passover and a new covenant.
We keep the feast with a clean heart, proclaiming his death until he comes.
opts.resolve: This Holy Week I will clear out the old yeast of one sin and prepare my heart for Communion.
homily: Dear friends, on the night of the first Passover the Israelites ate unleavened bread, and God told them to remove all leaven from their houses for seven days (Exodus 12:15). They left Egypt in haste, without time for the dough to rise. Every year the Pesaha appam, without yeast, reminds our families of that night.

Paul explains the meaning: clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch. For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed. Therefore let us celebrate the festival, not with the old yeast, the yeast of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth (1 Corinthians 5:7–8). The old yeast is the sin that has quietly spread through our life. Holy Week is the time to clear it out.

Jeremiah had promised: the days are surely coming, says the LORD, when I will make a new covenant (Jeremiah 31:31). Tonight that promise is kept. Jesus took the cup and said: this cup is the new covenant in my blood (1 Corinthians 11:25). The old covenant was sealed with the blood of animals. The new is sealed with the blood of the Son of God, given to us in the Holy Qurbana.

Paul adds: as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes (1 Corinthians 11:26). Every Holy Qurbana is not a new sacrifice but the one sacrifice of Calvary made present. That is why he says: examine yourselves, and only then eat of the bread and drink of the cup. The Psalm asks: what shall I return to the LORD for all his bounty to me? I will lift up the cup of salvation (Psalm 116:12–13).

So tonight let us break the Pesaha appam at home with grateful hearts. Let us remove the old yeast of one sin. Let us renew our baptismal promises before the Blessed Sacrament. And let us prepare, with a good confession, to receive the Lord worthily at Easter. Amen.

intro: Theme: “Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.”
The Passover lamb, Malachi's pure offering, the Body and Blood of the Lord given on the night he was betrayed, and the Lord who kneels to wash our feet.

q: The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you live: when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague shall destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
Clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch, as you really are unleavened. For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.
points.apply: Keep the home Pesaha tonight, and pray that the blood of the Lamb may protect your family.

points.h: A pure offering in every place
sub: From the rising of the sun to its setting.
q: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering; for my name is great among the nations, says the LORD of hosts.
For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.
points.apply: Give the Lord your best tonight: come early, prepared and reconciled.

sub: On the night he was betrayed.
Do this in remembrance of me.
q: The days are surely coming, says the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
for this is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
points.apply: Receive Communion tonight with a clean heart, and pray for the priests who make the Lord present for you.

q: Let a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.
points.apply: Do one humble service at home tonight, and watch one hour with the Lord.

concl: The Lamb of God gives us his Body and Blood, and the Lord of all kneels at our feet: the altar and the basin belong together.
Having loved his own, he loved them to the end; let us receive him worthily, serve one another, and watch with him tonight.
2027-03-25.resolve: Come to the one Qurbana, keep the home Pesaha, do one humble service, and watch one hour.
